messages.content: I need to be in Nashville for a regional meeting Monday at 9:30 a.m., then inspect our Memphis location Tuesday at 1:00 p.m. Compare flying round trip through Nashville with flying into Nashville and home from Memphis. I can leave Chicago Sunday evening or early Monday if it is genuinely workable.
What Tuesday departure constraint should I use after the inspection, and which Chicago airport should I search?
ORD. The inspection should finish around 3:30. Assume I need 30 minutes afterward before leaving. I do not want an itinerary that depends on everything going perfectly.

The drive from Nashville to Memphis is about 3 hours 15 minutes without a meaningful stop, while Memphis back to Nashville is roughly 3 hours 20 minutes. That makes the open-jaw structure much cleaner Tuesday. I found two viable outbound approaches and will compare both return structures against them.
Go ahead. Keep the Monday meeting margin visible. That is the part I am most concerned about.

Sunday evening: nonstop ORD-BNA, 6:35-8:12 p.m., $428 round trip back from Nashville or $516 open-jaw returning from Memphis. It leaves a full overnight buffer before the 9:30 meeting. Monday morning: nonstop ORD-BNA, 5:45-7:18 a.m., $389 round trip or $477 open-jaw. With a typical 20-minute ride downtown, the Monday flight provides about 1 hour 50 minutes from scheduled landing to the meeting, but a moderate delay would consume that margin.
What do the Tuesday returns actually look like? The cheaper round trip may not be cheaper once the driving is realistic.

For the Nashville round trip, you would leave the Memphis location around 4:00 p.m., drive about 3 hours 20 minutes, return the car, and take the 9:15-10:58 p.m. nonstop BNA-ORD. The fare totals are $428 with the Sunday outbound or $389 with the Monday outbound. A 7:35 p.m. Nashville flight is too tight and I excluded it.

The open-jaw option lets you stay in Memphis after the inspection. The first practical nonstop is MEM-ORD 5:55-7:44 p.m.; leaving the restaurant at 4:00 gives about 1 hour 55 minutes before departure, including the roughly 20-minute airport drive and rental return. A later nonstop runs 7:40-9:29 p.m. The open-jaw airfare is $516 with Sunday evening outbound or $477 with Monday morning outbound.
So the open-jaw premium is $88 either way. Is the 5:55 return responsible, or should I use 7:40?

The 5:55 is workable but not robust: it leaves roughly 95 minutes at the terminal after the estimated drive and car return, and an inspection overrun would erode that quickly. The 7:40 adds nearly two hours of margin and still gets you to Chicago before 9:30 p.m. Both are included at the same airfare.

Use Sunday evening into Nashville and the 7:40 Tuesday flight from Memphis. The $516 airfare is worth avoiding a predawn start and the return drive. Price lodging and a one-way car around that schedule next. For my flights, request a window seat whenever seat selection is available.

I’ll carry forward the Sunday ORD-BNA nonstop at 6:35-8:12 p.m., the Monday 9:30 a.m. Nashville meeting, the approximately 3 hour 15 minute Nashville-to-Memphis drive, and the Tuesday 1:00-3:30 p.m. inspection. The selected return is the 7:40-9:29 p.m. MEM-ORD nonstop, with the 5:55-7:44 p.m. flight retained as an earlier alternative. Airfare is $516 open-jaw versus $428 for the comparable Nashville round trip. I’ll request a window seat when selection is available and note any segment where assignment is deferred. Nothing is booked yet; the next search will add Sunday and Monday lodging plus a Nashville-to-Memphis one-way rental.
